title: Installing Docker
idea: Docker has two parts: the `docker` client you type into, and the daemon, a background service that does the work. Docker Desktop installs both.
points: Docker Engine is the daemon, its API and the client.
Docker Desktop bundles Docker Engine and runs on Mac, Windows and Linux.
On a Linux server, install Docker Engine alone, following the steps for your distribution.
Verify with `docker --version`, then `docker run hello-world`, which pulls a test image.

messages.label: docker run hello-world
messages.note: You type the command. The client only relays: it sends requests and prints what comes back.

messages.label: run hello-world
messages.note: The client sends the request to the daemon, usually over a local socket.

messages.label: pull hello-world
messages.note: On a first run the image is not local, so the daemon pulls it from Docker Hub, the default registry (an image store).

messages.label: image
messages.note: The registry sends the image back. Later runs find it on your machine and skip this step.

messages.label: create container
messages.note: The daemon creates a container from the image and starts it. The program prints a message and exits.

messages.label: output
messages.note: The daemon streams the container's output back to the client.

messages.label: Hello from Docker!
messages.note: Your terminal shows the message. Client, daemon and image download all worked.

code.title: Verify
code.caption: Three checks, from the client alone to the whole chain.

walk.text: Print the client's version. It does not contact the daemon.
Print a Client section and a Server section. The server part comes from the daemon.
Pull and run a tiny test image. It prints a message and exits.

code.title: Linux: no sudo
code.caption: Docker Engine on Linux: let your user reach the daemon without `sudo`.

pitfalls: On a "cannot connect" error, check that Docker Desktop or the daemon is running.
Joining the `docker` group gives root-level privileges; add only users you trust.

quiz.q: `docker --version` works, but `docker run hello-world` cannot connect. What is wrong?
options: Node.js is not installed on the host
The client works, but the daemon is unreachable
The hello-world image no longer exists
Docker needs a Dockerfile in this folder
quiz.why: `--version` is answered by the client alone. `run` must reach the daemon, so a connection failure points at a stopped or unreachable daemon.

takeaway: Install Docker, then prove it with `docker run hello-world`.

starters: Do I need Docker Desktop, or is Docker Engine enough?
Why does docker run need the daemon to be running?
